02-networking/what-is-a-network.q: A video call feels delayed even though the connection can transfer large files quickly. Which measurement best describes that delay?
options: Latency
Bandwidth
The Wi-Fi network name
The number of open browser tabs
02-networking/what-is-a-network.explain: Latency measures how long data takes to travel; bandwidth describes how much data a connection can carry over time.
02-networking/what-is-a-network.review: Bandwidth vs. latency — two different kinds of "speed"

02-networking/routing-basics.q: A device has no more specific route for an outside destination. Where does it usually send the packet?
options: To a DNS record
To its default gateway
To every device on the local network
Directly to the destination without using a router
02-networking/routing-basics.explain: A default route points to a gateway for destinations without a more specific matching route.
02-networking/routing-basics.review: The default gateway: your network's exit door

02-networking/ip-addresses.q: What can DHCP provide to a device joining a network?
options: A permanent domain name for every device
Encryption for every application
An automatically assigned IP configuration
A guarantee that its address can never change
02-networking/ip-addresses.explain: DHCP can automatically assign network settings such as an IP address; an assigned address can change.
02-networking/ip-addresses.review: Static vs. dynamic IPs — and DHCP

02-networking/subnetting-and-cidr.q: How many total IPv4 addresses are in a /24 block?
02-networking/subnetting-and-cidr.explain: A /24 leaves eight address bits, giving 2⁸, or 256 total addresses. Usable host counts depend on the subnet and its use.

02-networking/nat-and-port-forwarding.q: What does a port-forwarding rule generally do?
options: Sends matching incoming traffic to a chosen internal address and port
Encrypts all traffic on the network
Assigns a domain name to every device
Stops the chosen internal service from receiving traffic
02-networking/nat-and-port-forwarding.explain: Port forwarding maps selected incoming traffic to an internal service, potentially making that service reachable from outside.
02-networking/nat-and-port-forwarding.review: Port forwarding: deliberately opening a door

02-networking/ports.q: Why does a client typically use an ephemeral port when connecting to a server?
options: To replace the destination IP address
To identify the client side of a connection
To guarantee that the traffic is encrypted
To convert UDP traffic into TCP
02-networking/ports.explain: The client typically selects a temporary source port; the server listens on its destination port.
02-networking/ports.review: Ephemeral ports — the other side of every connection

02-networking/packets.q: What happens during encapsulation as data moves down a network stack?
options: The application removes all addressing information
Every device receives the same private key
Each layer adds its own protocol information around the data
The destination changes the source data into a domain name
02-networking/packets.explain: Layers add protocol information to the data they carry. The receiver processes the corresponding layers in reverse.

02-networking/switches-and-vlans.q: What does a VLAN allow an organization to do on compatible network equipment?
options: Make a cable carry unlimited bandwidth
Remove the need for IP addresses
Encrypt every application automatically
Separate devices into logical network segments
02-networking/switches-and-vlans.explain: VLANs provide logical segmentation on compatible switching equipment. Traffic between segments still depends on routing and policy.
02-networking/switches-and-vlans.review: VLANs: one physical switch, several logical networks

02-networking/protocols.q: Why do two systems need an agreed network protocol?
options: So they can interpret messages and follow compatible rules
So they always use the same operating system
So no network failure can occur
So every message remains secret by default
02-networking/protocols.explain: A protocol specifies rules for communication, such as message formats and expected behavior. Encryption depends on the protocol and its use.
02-networking/protocols.review: Just an agreed set of rules

02-networking/tcp-vs-udp.q: Which sequence describes a typical TCP connection handshake?
options: ACK, ACK, SYN
SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK
GET, POST, DELETE
DNS, HTTP, TLS
02-networking/tcp-vs-udp.explain: A client sends SYN, the server responds with SYN-ACK, and the client acknowledges with ACK.

02-networking/wireless-networking-basics.q: A nearby access point uses the same network name as a trusted café. What concern does this illustrate?
options: A VLAN automatically shares its passwords
A router has necessarily failed
A rogue access point may be impersonating the trusted network
A matching name proves the network is authentic
02-networking/wireless-networking-basics.explain: An evil twin can copy a legitimate network name. The name alone does not establish who operates the access point.
02-networking/wireless-networking-basics.review: Evil twin attacks: a wireless-specific threat

02-networking/http-https.q: What does HTTPS add to HTTP when the connection is correctly established?
options: A guarantee that the website content is truthful
A guarantee that the server has no vulnerabilities
A requirement that every page be public
TLS protection for the connection
02-networking/http-https.explain: HTTPS uses TLS to protect data in transit and authenticate the server when certificate validation succeeds. It does not make the site itself trustworthy.

02-networking/firewalls-basics.q: What distinguishes a stateful firewall from a stateless packet filter?
options: It can use connection state when evaluating traffic
It makes every allowed application safe
It replaces the need for authentication
It always reads encrypted application content
02-networking/firewalls-basics.explain: A stateful firewall can track connection context; a stateless filter evaluates packets without that connection history.

02-networking/common-network-attacks-ove.q: What is a possible consequence of ARP spoofing on a local network?
options: A domain name is permanently deleted
Traffic may be sent to a device impersonating the gateway
Every encrypted message becomes readable automatically
A browser installs an operating system update
02-networking/common-network-attacks-ove.explain: Forged ARP messages can associate an IP address with an attacker-controlled MAC address and redirect local traffic.
02-networking/common-network-attacks-ove.review: ARP spoofing: lying about who you are on the local network

02-networking/network-troubleshooting-to.q: Which tool is intended for asking a DNS resolver about a name?
options: A text editor
A file compression tool
nslookup or dig
A screen brightness control
02-networking/network-troubleshooting-to.explain: nslookup and dig can request DNS records. Record the question and response before deciding what the result means.

02-networking/dns-lab.q: Which DNS record type identifies authoritative name servers for a zone?
options: A
MX
AAAA
NS
02-networking/dns-lab.explain: NS records identify name servers for a zone; A and AAAA records provide addresses and MX records identify mail exchangers.

options: A logical network built over an underlying network
A replacement for all physical infrastructure
A guarantee that all workloads are isolated
A physical cable connecting every device directly
02-networking/cloud-and-modern-networkin.explain: An overlay creates a logical network over underlying infrastructure. Its actual connectivity and isolation depend on configuration.

02-networking/network-certifications-car.q: How can you demonstrate networking skills to a prospective employer?
options: Claim that a certificate guarantees a job
Document a project or home lab and explain the decisions and results
List every tool without describing how you used it
Share credentials to a production network
02-networking/network-certifications-car.explain: A documented project or lab gives you concrete evidence to discuss alongside relevant learning and certifications.

02-networking/practical-packet-lab.q: In a packet capture, what does a TCP SYN followed by SYN-ACK suggest?
options: A DNS response has been cached forever
HTTP content is necessarily unencrypted
A TCP connection is being established
The capture contains every packet on the internet
02-networking/practical-packet-lab.explain: SYN and SYN-ACK are the first two steps of the TCP handshake; the client normally follows with an ACK.

02-networking/dns.q: Which DNS record type names a mail exchanger for a domain?
options: AAAA
MX
CNAME
PTR
02-networking/dns.explain: An MX record names a mail exchanger and provides a preference value. A and AAAA records provide addresses; CNAME identifies an alias target.

02-networking/dns-response-troubleshooti.q: A resolver returns NOERROR with no AAAA answer for a name. What is the careful next interpretation?
options: The domain can never have any records
The server has definitely been compromised
Check the question and response; the name may exist without an AAAA record
Assume all network traffic is blocked
02-networking/dns-response-troubleshooti.explain: An empty answer needs context. It can represent no data for the requested type; check the question and authority section before drawing broader conclusions.
02-networking/dns-response-troubleshooti.review: Read the response, not just the empty answer

18-ai-security/mcp-tool-authorization.q: A document tells a read-only invoice assistant to send the invoice outside the company. What should enforce the boundary?
options: The document author
The model approving its own call
A trusted tool gateway checking the authenticated actor and task
An approved field supplied in the tool arguments
18-ai-security/mcp-tool-authorization.explain: Document text and proposed tool arguments are untrusted. The gateway must reject actions beyond the actual task even if the model proposes them.

18-ai-security/rag-tenant-isolation.q: A private document from another tenant is the closest search match. What should the retrieval system do?
options: Exclude it before model context is built
Send it to the model but hide its citation
Let the model decide whether the user should see it
Use it if the question names that tenant
18-ai-security/rag-tenant-isolation.explain: Similarity does not grant access. Filter using trusted identity and document permissions before building context; hiding a citation later cannot undo exposure.
18-ai-security/rag-tenant-isolation.review: Filter before ranking and context construction

18-ai-security/ai-security-release-gates.q: Why should an AI security evaluation include legitimate tasks as well as attacks?
options: To guarantee that no future attack can succeed
To remove the need for authorization tests
To make every refusal count as a successful defense
To catch a system that blocks useful work instead of preserving safe use
18-ai-security/ai-security-release-gates.explain: Measure legitimate-task success separately from unauthorized actions. A deny-everything policy is not a useful fix, and a small evaluation cannot prove future safety.

22-devsecops-appsec/what-is-devsecops.q: A team can add only one security control this week. What is a useful first step?
options: Buy a scanner before choosing a risk
Pick one risky feature, name an owner, and agree on a check
Wait until every developer has a security certification
Make the security team responsible for every code change
22-devsecops-appsec/what-is-devsecops.explain: Start with a small control tied to a real risk. An owner and a repeatable check make the improvement easier to deliver and verify.

22-devsecops-appsec/shift-left-vs-shift-.q: A team adds code review before release. What should happen to its production security checks?
options: Stop them because review happens earlier
Use them only after a confirmed breach
Keep them: early review and production feedback catch different problems
Replace monitoring with developer training
22-devsecops-appsec/shift-left-vs-shift-.explain: Earlier checks reduce rework, but live configuration, behavior, and new threats still need attention. Use feedback before and after release.
22-devsecops-appsec/shift-left-vs-shift-.review: Why mature programs need both, not one or the other

22-devsecops-appsec/security-requirement.q: Which acceptance criterion can verify the invoice ownership rule?
options: The invoice page looks secure
The application uses a popular framework
A scanner reports no critical findings
Customer A can read A’s invoice, while customer B cannot read it
22-devsecops-appsec/security-requirement.explain: A testable requirement names both allowed and denied behavior. A successful login or a green scan does not prove ownership checks work.
22-devsecops-appsec/security-requirement.review: Write acceptance criteria that can fail

22-devsecops-appsec/threat-modeling-sdlc.q: Before choosing controls for a new file-upload feature, what should the team identify?
options: The data flow, trust boundaries, and ways the feature could be abused
Only the final penetration-test date
A scanner that guarantees no vulnerabilities
Every possible threat to every system in the company
22-devsecops-appsec/threat-modeling-sdlc.explain: A small threat model follows the feature’s data and trust boundaries, then turns plausible abuse into controls and verification tasks.

22-devsecops-appsec/secure-code-review.q: An invoice query now uses bound SQL parameters. What still needs a separate check?
options: Whether the invoice ID is printed in the URL
Whether the signed-in actor is allowed to read that invoice
Whether the database has any indexes
Whether every denied request returns an invoice anyway
22-devsecops-appsec/secure-code-review.explain: Parameter binding separates data from SQL syntax. Authorization separately checks whether this actor may access this object.

22-devsecops-appsec/sast-dast-sca.q: You need to identify known vulnerabilities in third-party packages. Which check is the best starting point?
options: DAST against only the login page
A code formatter
SCA against the application’s dependencies
A screenshot review
22-devsecops-appsec/sast-dast-sca.explain: Software composition analysis identifies component risk. Confirm affected versions and context; it does not prove the whole application is secure.

22-devsecops-appsec/iac-security-scannin.q: An IaC scan finds a storage bucket configured for public access. What is the useful next step?
options: Ignore it until someone downloads data
Assume every bucket must have the same policy
Treat a green code scan as proof the cloud account is safe
Check the intended access, fix the template if needed, and verify the deployed setting
22-devsecops-appsec/iac-security-scannin.explain: IaC checks can catch risky settings before deployment. The intended policy and the actual deployed state still need verification.
22-devsecops-appsec/iac-security-scannin.review: Why IaC scanning catches what runtime cloud scanning catches too late

22-devsecops-appsec/cicd-security.q: What is a useful way to reduce the impact of a compromised CI job?
options: Give its token only the permissions the job needs
Give every workflow an administrator token
Put deployment secrets in pull-request logs
Trust every contribution because the repository is public
22-devsecops-appsec/cicd-security.explain: Least-privilege job tokens limit what a compromised job can do. Untrusted code, secrets, and privileged deployment steps also need clear boundaries.

22-devsecops-appsec/container-image-and-.q: A container image has a valid signature. What does that establish?
options: It has no exploitable vulnerabilities
It is associated with the verified signer and has not changed since signing
Its application enforces every authorization rule
It will remain safe without updates
22-devsecops-appsec/container-image-and-.explain: A signature helps verify origin and integrity under your trust policy. It does not replace vulnerability review, safe configuration, or application testing.
22-devsecops-appsec/container-image-and-.review: Image signing and provenance — verifying what actually gets deployed

22-devsecops-appsec/secrets-supply-chain.q: A valid API key was committed, then removed in a later commit. What should happen next?
options: Keep using it because the latest file is clean
Rename the repository
Revoke or rotate it and investigate exposure, including repository history
Hide the commit message and close the finding
22-devsecops-appsec/secrets-supply-chain.explain: Removing a key from the current file does not revoke copies in history, logs, caches, or clones. Invalidate the exposed credential and check its use.

22-devsecops-appsec/sbom-and-software-bi.q: A new vulnerability affects a transitive dependency. How can a current SBOM help?
options: Automatically prove that exploitation is impossible
Replace every dependency update
Prove all code is free of licensing issues
Find which built applications include the affected component for further assessment
22-devsecops-appsec/sbom-and-software-bi.explain: An SBOM inventories components, including indirect dependencies. Use it to locate affected builds, then assess exposure and remediation.

22-devsecops-appsec/vulnerability-manage.q: Two findings have similar severity scores. What helps decide which to fix first?
options: Exposure, reachability, exploitation evidence, and business impact
Only the alphabetical order of the package names
Only which scanner reported the most findings
Whether the finding has a longer description
22-devsecops-appsec/vulnerability-manage.explain: A severity score is one input. Actual exposure, reachable vulnerable behavior, active exploitation, and impact make prioritization more useful.
22-devsecops-appsec/vulnerability-manage.review: CVSS alone is genuinely insufficient for prioritization

22-devsecops-appsec/security-champions-p.q: What makes a security champions program useful to a development team?
options: Making volunteers solely accountable for all security defects
Giving champions time, training, support, and a route to the security team
Adding responsibilities without changing workload
Replacing specialist review with a champion title
22-devsecops-appsec/security-champions-p.explain: Champions help teams apply security in daily work. They need support and time; a title alone does not replace specialist help or shared responsibility.
22-devsecops-appsec/security-champions-p.review: What makes a Champions program succeed, versus fail

22-devsecops-appsec/metrics-that-matter.q: A dashboard shows twice as many scanner findings this month. What can you conclude?
options: The team is definitely twice as insecure
The program has definitely become twice as effective
Investigate context: coverage, meaningful risk, remediation time, and recurring defects
Stop measuring security because counts can change
22-devsecops-appsec/metrics-that-matter.explain: A raw finding count can change with scan coverage or noise. Pair activity with measures that explain risk and whether fixes last.

22-devsecops-appsec/building-appsec-prog.q: What belongs in a realistic first 90-day AppSec plan?
options: A promise to remove every vulnerability
A tool purchase with no owner or success measure
A ban on releases until the whole backlog is empty
A small risk-based scope, owners, milestones, and ways to verify improvement
22-devsecops-appsec/building-appsec-prog.explain: Start with a scope the team can deliver. Clear ownership, a few useful controls, and evidence of outcomes support the next iteration.

22-devsecops-appsec/appsec-tooling-and-o.q: Three scanners report the same underlying issue. What should orchestration help the team do?
options: Group related evidence, assign an owner, and track one coordinated remediation
Automatically discard every repeated report
Count each report as a separate fixed vulnerability
Assume the finding is false because tools agree
22-devsecops-appsec/appsec-tooling-and-o.explain: Deduplication reduces repeated work while preserving evidence. Ownership and a useful workflow matter more than collecting another dashboard.
22-devsecops-appsec/appsec-tooling-and-o.review: Why deduplication genuinely matters, not just for tidiness

22-devsecops-appsec/appsec-fix-verify-la.q: The Python lab passes with --reference. How do you verify your own edited starter?
options: The reference result is already enough
Run the unchanged tests without --reference and confirm both allowed and denied cases pass
Delete the failing ownership tests
Return None for every request
22-devsecops-appsec/appsec-fix-verify-la.explain: Reference mode runs the supplied worked implementation. The normal command tests your get_invoice function; legitimate access must work as well as denied access.

22-devsecops-appsec/appsec-program-lab.q: Which capstone evidence best connects a program plan to a working improvement?
options: A list of tools without configuration or results
A claim that the fictional company is certified
A reproducible finding, a reviewed fix, test results, and a documented remaining risk
A screenshot showing only the number of scans
22-devsecops-appsec/appsec-program-lab.explain: A program plan becomes more useful when it includes technical evidence. Show what changed, how you checked it, and the limits of the exercise.

22-devsecops-appsec/vulnerability-triage.q: A catalog lists a vulnerability as exploited, but you do not know whether your deployed version is affected. What should you do first?
options: Confirm the deployed component and exposure while arranging a mitigation path
Assume all assets are affected and close the investigation
Ignore the catalog until a scanner produces a higher score
Declare the finding fixed without examining the deployment
22-devsecops-appsec/vulnerability-triage.explain: Known exploitation is an urgent signal to investigate. Applicability and exposure still need evidence, and teams can prepare mitigation in parallel.

22-devsecops-appsec/verify-vulnerability.q: An upgrade passes CI. What evidence best supports closing an affected production finding?
options: A screenshot of the pull request alone
Evidence the fixed build reached the affected asset, plus targeted checks and a record of remaining risk
The developer says the dependency is probably unused
A lower backlog count
22-devsecops-appsec/verify-vulnerability.explain: A source fix is not necessarily deployed everywhere. Check the affected asset, relevant behavior and residual exposure before closing the finding.
